title: Multiplying a 2-Digit Number by a 1-Digit Number
seo_title: Grade 3 Multiplying 2-Digit by 1-Digit Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 3.4G, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.4G use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number. Strategies may include mental math, partial products, and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.4G: multiply by multiples of 10, area models, partial products, the distributive property, the standard algorithm with regrouping and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply the tens and the ones, then add.
key_sub: 6 × 47 = (6 × 40) + (6 × 7) = 240 + 42 = 282. In the standard algorithm, regroup and add the extra tens.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Break the 2-digit number into tens and ones: 47 = 40 + 7.
  • Multiply each part, then add the partial products: 6 × 47 = (6 × 40) + (6 × 7) = 240 + 42 = 282.
  • An area model shows the two parts as two rectangles.
  • In the standard algorithm, multiply the ones first. If the product is 10 or more, regroup the tens and add them after you multiply the tens.

Examples

Example

Find 38 × 4 with the standard algorithm.

Ones: 4 × 8 = 32. Write 2, regroup 3 tens.

Tens: 4 × 3 = 12 tens. Add the 3 regrouped tens: 15 tens.

Write 15 tens as 150 and add the 2.

Answer: 152

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying only the ones: 6 × 47 = 242Multiply both the tens and the ones.
Forgetting the regrouped tensWrite the regrouped ten above the tens column and add it.
Writing 6 × 4 = 24 instead of 6 × 40 = 240The 4 in 47 means 4 tens, so the partial product is 240.

faq.a: Use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply a 2-digit number by a 1-digit number. Strategies include mental math, partial products and the properties of operations.
The products you get when you multiply the tens and the ones separately, like 6 × 40 = 240 and 6 × 7 = 42. Their sum is the answer.

faq.q: How does an area model help?
faq.a: It shows the number split into tens and ones as two rectangles, so you can see both partial products.

faq.q: When do Texas students learn the standard algorithm?
faq.a: Grade 3 students start with a 2-digit by 1-digit number (TEKS 3.4G). Grade 4 extends it to bigger numbers.
